**Eight usual assumptions and their negations**

1. Skip connections on the direct edge (0→3) always help. If false, they help less once a deep conv path exists.
2. Convs beat everything else on every edge. If false, pooling or 1x1 on one edge can substitute when capacity elsewhere is high.
3. More conv3x3 edges is monotonically better. If false, parallel strong paths are redundant and the second one adds little.
4. Removing an edge always hurts. If false, removal costs little when strong convs exist elsewhere.
5. Upgrading an op is good regardless of context. If false, the upgrade gains vanish or reverse when a skip already supplies the shortcut.
6. Edits on edges downstream of node 1 matter independently of edge 0. If false, they become inert when node 1 is cut off.
7. Two skips are better than one. If false, parallel skips are redundant.
8. Cheap ops (pool, 1x1) always lose to conv3x3. If false, they lose much less, or win, beside strong neighbours.

The 20 hypotheses below are built from these negations.
